tldr: Google's Antigravity SDK added local-model support on Oct 14, pitched as a token-efficiency and code-privacy gain. A paper on Oct 23 then targeted the harness itself, where reasoning is re-invoked after tool feedback even when the next action is already fixed.
whats_new: A Hacker News post on Oct 28 claims a Lisp coding agent beats Codex by 10x on token efficiency; the claim is unverified and the linked source is a social post.
why_it_matters: Agent token spend is shifting from model choice to harness design: how often the loop re-invokes reasoning and whether work runs locally.

status.detail: Three loosely related items; only one is a peer-style method, and the latest 10x claim lacks published methodology in the bundle.

beats.headline: Antigravity SDK adds local model support
beats.summary: Agentic workflows can run on the developer's machine, with cloud models mixable in.

beats.headline: HarnessMM cuts redundant reasoning calls in agent harnesses
beats.summary: Targets re-invocation of reasoning after tool feedback when the next action is already determined.

beats.headline: Lisp coding agent claims 10x token efficiency over Codex
beats.summary: A social-media claim surfaced on Hacker News, with no benchmark details in the feed item.

open_questions: Does the Lisp agent's 10x figure come with a published task set and token-counting method?
Does HarnessMM report token savings on a public coding-agent benchmark, and at what accuracy cost?
Does Antigravity publish token or cost comparisons between local and cloud models?
take_for_builders: Log tokens per completed task in your own harness and test whether skipping a reasoning call after tool output changes success rate before trusting any vendor or social-media multiplier.

day_captions.72f3ee5066aaa64d: Frames local execution as a token-efficiency and code-privacy option for agent SDKs.
day_captions.ac57fbd36999bb7e: Moves the efficiency question from the model to harness control flow.
day_captions.9f96f9f3a384b51e: Adds a 10x efficiency claim versus Codex, unverified in the cited item.
